citations.evidenceText:
Tool Centre Point :

•  The Tool Center Point (TCP) calibration defines the exact position of the
   effective working point of the end-effector with respect to the robot flange.
•   In the four-point calibration method, the robot tool tip is brought to the same
   physical reference point from four different orientations.
•  By analyzing these four poses, the controller computes the
   intersection point corresponding to the actual TCP location.
•  Accurate TCP calibration is essential for achieving high positioning accuracy and
   repeatability during pick-and-drop operations.
•  An incorrectly calibrated TCP can result in positioning
    errors, grasp failures and reduced process reliability in
   robotic applications.



                                                                                                           9

citations.locator: Lecture L57, physical page 1812, printed footer 10: Record differing orientations and compute flange-relative XYZ.
citations.evidenceText:
Calibration Procedure :

•  Step 1: Select the desired tool number in the Tool/Base calibration menu.
•  Step 2: Choose a fixed reference point on the worktable or calibration pin.
•  Step 3: Move the tool tip to the reference point and record the first position.
•  Step 4: Change the robot orientation while keeping the tool tip on the same
   point and record the second position.
•  Step 5: Repeat the process for the third orientation.
•  Step 6: Record a fourth pose with a different orientation.
•  Step 7: KUKA System Software automatically calculates
   the TCP coordinates (X, Y, Z) relative to the robot flange.
•  Step 8: Verify the calibration by performing linear
   motions and checking for positional deviations.


                                                                                                          10

citations.evidenceText:
Camera Calibration :
•  Camera calibration is the process of determining the intrinsic and extrinsic
   parameters of the camera to establish the relationship between image
   coordinates and real-world coordinates.
•  Accurate calibration improves measurement precision and enables reliable
    object localization in robotic applications.
•  The calibration procedure is typically performed using a checkerboard pattern
   and OpenCV calibration algorithms.
•  Multiple images of the calibration target are captured from different
    orientations to compute the camera parameters and
   minimize reprojection error.
•  Parameters Obtained
   – Focal length (𝑓𝑥, 𝑓𝑦), Principal point (𝑐𝑥, 𝑐𝑦), Distortion
        coefficients, Rotation matrix, Translation vector.

                                                                                                          18

citations.locator: Lecture L57, physical page 1830, printed footer 28: Camera/marker/robot frame relation.
citations.evidenceText:
Coordinate Transformation :

•  Coordinate transformation is the process of converting object positions
   obtained from the camera coordinate system into the robot coordinate system.
•  Since the camera and robot operate in different reference frames, a common
   transformation framework is required to ensure accurate object localization and
   manipulation.
•   In the present system, the ArUco marker acts as an intermediate reference
   frame between the Intel RealSense camera and the KUKA robot.
•  The object coordinates are first determined in the camera
   frame and then transformed into the marker frame.
•  After applying the marker offset, the final coordinates are
   obtained in the robot base frame, which are used for
   motion execution.
